results.content: * [Català](https://ca.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Graves "Alex Graves – Catalan"). * [Article](/wiki/Alex_Graves_(computer_scientist) "View the content page [c]"). At the [Dalle Molle Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research](/wiki/Dalle_Molle_Institute_for_Artificial_Intelligence_Research "Dalle Molle Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research"), Graves trained [long short-term memory](/wiki/Long_short-term_memory "Long short-term memory") (LSTM) neural networks by a novel method called [connectionist temporal classification](/wiki/Connectionist_temporal_classification "Connectionist temporal classification") (CTC).[[5]](#cite_note-graves2006-5) This method outperformed traditional [speech recognition](/wiki/Speech_recognition "Speech recognition") models in certain applications.[[6]](#cite_note-fernandez2007keyword-6) In 2009, his CTC-trained LSTM was the first [recurrent neural network](/wiki/Recurrent_neural_network "Recurrent neural network") (RNN) to win pattern recognition contests, winning several competitions in connected [handwriting recognition](/wiki/Handwriting_recognition "Handwriting recognition").[[7]](#cite_note-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8) [Google](/wiki/Google "Google") uses CTC-trained LSTM for speech recognition on the [smartphone](/wiki/Smartphone "Smartphone").[[9]](#cite_note-GoogleVoiceTranscription-9)[[10]](#cite_note-GoogleVoiceSearch-10). Graves is also the creator of [neural Turing machines](/wiki/Neural_Turing_machine "Neural Turing machine")[[11]](#cite_note-MyUser_Https:_May_17_2016c-11) and the closely related [differentiable neural computer](/wiki/Differentiable_neural_computer "Differentiable neural computer").[[12]](#cite_note-DNCnature2016-12)[[13]](#cite_note-13) In 2023, he wrote the paper *Bayesian Flow Networks*.[[14]](#cite_note-14) He currently works as a Staff Research Scientist at [InstaDeep](/wiki/InstaDeep "InstaDeep").[[15]](#cite_note-15)[[16]](#cite_note-16) He was previously a research scientist at [Google DeepMind](/wiki/Google_DeepMind "Google DeepMind") in London.[[17]](#cite_note-17). 1. ^ [***a***](#cite_ref-gs_1-0) [***b***](#cite_ref-gs_1-1) [Alex Graves](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=DaFHynwAAAAJ) publications indexed by [Google Scholar](/wiki/Google_Scholar "Google Scholar").
